name: switcher
description: A row of equal-width peers that becomes a single column when the switcher itself is narrower than its threshold — driven by a container query on its own inline size, never by the viewport, so the same markup is correct full-bleed, in a sidebar and in a dialog

a11y.notes: Layout-only primitive; no semantic role required. The flip is a CSS layout change with no DOM reorder, so the reading order is identical in both arrangements.

notes: data-threshold names a length on the CANON ladder (sm 40rem · md 48rem · lg 64rem · xl 80rem, FAQIR-SPEC §15) measured on the switcher's own inline size — not on the viewport. A switcher in a 24rem sidebar is a column even on a 4K display, which is the point.

Nothing here takes a tier suffix. data-gap-md would make a container-driven component viewport-driven again; if a layout genuinely needs to answer to the page width, that is a pattern's job (§15 doctrine 3), not a switcher's.

The children become equal-width columns above the threshold (flex-basis: 0), so switcher suits peers — two panels, a row of actions, a form's field pair. For items of unequal importance that merely need to reflow, use cluster; for a fixed column count, use grid.

The root is a query container (container-type: inline-size, container-name: faqir-switcher) and therefore takes its width from its parent. Nested switchers each measure their own column: the inner one answers to the space the outer one gave it.
